findings.claim: useMemberTarget keeps the last evaluation in `held` and never clears it on a target change, so after switching a member target away and back, the same key matches the old result and the app is ready with stale members before the re-evaluation finishes.
findings.impact: After switching Video or Reading from a Smart Collection with free text to another target and back, in one page visit, requests go out immediately with the earlier member set, not the set the collection holds now. Members added or removed in between are not reflected until the re-evaluation completes, and the requests then fire a second time when the new evaluation replaces the old one.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/appshell/useMemberTarget.ts:27 (held state), :33 (setHeld only on resolution), :41 (evaluation = held when held.key === key, and key is null for a target with no kinds or no target, so the old entry is not cleared). Sequence: A evaluates (held.key = A-key); target switches to default (key = null, evaluation = null); target switches back to A (key = A-key again, so evaluation = the old result, evaluating = false, ready = true). The effect at :29-38 then re-evaluates A, and a new held object with the same key changes requests identity. The hook's docstring says a result that outlives its target is dropped; the code does not do that. Introduced by the feature branch, not touched by any fix commit since r6 (96a1fd8, d216d54, 424ee41, 0af8d49, 0299394, 6c312bd).
findings.repro: Not reproduced: traced in code only. Steps: in Video, pick a member target, let its evaluation settle, pick the default target, pick the member target again, and observe that the first shelf requests carry the earlier file_ids before the second evaluation request returns. No test covers a return to an earlier target.

bucket_proposal.reason: The ids sent are members of an earlier successful evaluation of the same target, so I8's clauses about evaluated members and no requests before success are not literally broken. The States section's 'a target change restarts at evaluating' is prose, not an invariant id, so this is a wrong-behaviour finding without a declared invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Clear `held` when the key becomes null, or key the stored result by the attempt and target and drop it on a target change, so a return to a target always starts at evaluating.

potential_unspecified_behavior: Switching a member target away and back in one page visit reuses the earlier evaluation without re-evaluating (R7-1).

A Smart Collection named twice in `in:` (for example `in:"Weekly" in:weekly`) is evaluated twice in resolveInNames, because classifyNames does not deduplicate smart folders. This is harmless to the result but breaks the one-evaluation-per-name bound in SPEC-CORE-116 §10.
regression_risks: useMemberTarget's shared `held` state is the single source of a member target's readiness. Any new caller that switches targets inside one mount inherits R7-1 until it is fixed.

The in: lifecycle now has four dimensions (inKey, inRetryToken, resolutionGeneration, listedResolution) plus the continuation key. A future change to one of them without the others can recreate the stale-image-rows and count-of-zero defects that 96a1fd8 fixed.
